newsitem.title: UK: UK union body hails EU move on worker consultation.
newsitem.headline: UK union body hails EU move on worker consultation.

text.p: Britain's Trades Union Council (TUC), the umbrella group for UK unions, on Wednesday applauded a European Commission plan to extend employees' right to be consulted on company changes.
"We very much welcome today's (EC) proposals," TUC general secretary John Monks said in a statement.
"Growing integration in line with the completion of the internal market means that we need to ensure the possibility of proper consultation in all companies of medium size and above," he said.

The plan put forward by European Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn, would oblige companies to set up national systems for consulting workers on decisions that affect their jobs, the Commission said nPF0400495.
The TUC said firms with 50 employees or more were likely to have to consult workers on matters such as company performance and employment prospects under the new rules.

The TUC welcomed the move because it would give British workers a legal right to be consulted and allow workers to be more actively involved. UK bosses and employees currently have no national consultation laws and contact each other on a voluntary basis.

"These proposals provide a golden opportunity for rationalising the UK's current complex patchwork of existing requirements and bringing the UK into line with European requirements that the previous (Conservative) government had ignored," Monks said.

Most EU member states already have national laws which provide for works councils. But British business is likely to interpret the move as an attempt by European authorities to shackle UK firms with inflexible employment laws.

Prime Minister Tony Blair has pledged to sign up to the EU's Social Chapter on workers' rights at an EU summit on June 16. One of the charter's two existing regulations is the European Works Council Directive which requires large companies operating in Europe to set up 'works councils' for consultation and providing workers with prior information on corporate changes.

The EU is keen to beef up the employee's role in a company's operations. The Commission's latest proposals for workers' consultation rights may kick-start a long-stalled plan to establish a European Company Statute, which includes provision for employee information, consultation and participation, the TUC noted.
European law makers are increasingly being urged by governments and unions to make employment and workers' rights a top priority.
